neverPrintsDatabaseUrl.evidence: classify() derives only a category from the hostname; emit() re-serializes and hard-exits(3) if the DSN string appears in the output.

neverPrintsCredentials.evidence: the catch block prints only e.code, never e.message (which can embed host/user).

doesNotFetchCustomerRows.evidence: queries hit pg_roles, pg_class, pg_proc, information_schema.role_table_grants only.

strictQueryWhitelist.gap: Queries are hardcoded but there is NO enforced whitelist/validator. Nothing structurally prevents a future edit from adding a mutating or customer-row statement.

statementTimeout.gap: No statement_timeout, no lock_timeout, no idle_in_transaction_session_timeout. A blocking catalog query could hold a session open against a production database.

requiresExplicitConnectFlag.evidence: const CONNECT = process.argv.includes('--connect'); default path never opens a pool.

readOnlyTransactionEnforced.evidence: 'set session characteristics as transaction read only' + 'begin read only' + final rollback.

additionalGapsForE12Scope: No explicit owner-authorization state: --connect alone is treated as authorization.
search_path is not pinned (§4 requires no search-path trust).
Leak guard only tests the exact DSN string; it does not test the username/password substrings independently.
Covers P9.4.1 ONLY. The partner payout migration (2026-07-11_05) is not inspected at all.
Does not read the Supabase migration-history table, so it cannot reconcile history vs objects (§7).
Object inspection is shallow: table names + RLS flags only. No columns, types, defaults, PKs, unique constraints, FKs, indexes, ownership, or policy expressions (§5B/5C).
Function inspection is name-only: no prosecdef (SECURITY DEFINER) check, no proconfig/search_path check (§5E).
Does not record PostgreSQL major version, current-role category, SSL mode category, or a target fingerprint (§8).
migrationState has no INCOMPATIBLE_EXISTING_STATE or UNVERIFIABLE class (§5 requires 5 classes).
strengtheningDeferredReason: E1.2 halted at §1. Strengthening the tool means writing code and running tsc/vitest; both would be measured against a repository that a foreign agent is concurrently rewriting, producing a volatile and uncertifiable green. Deferred to the unblocked run.
conclusion: The existing tool is SAFE ENOUGH TO NOT MUTATE, but NOT SUFFICIENT for the E1.2 mandate. It must be strengthened (timeouts, enforced whitelist, migration history, deep object/RLS/grant/function inspection, partner payout coverage) BEFORE it is pointed at a production Supabase target.
